nodes.name: Visual biomarkers for predicting fruit ripeness and sensory quality: A critical review
nodes.venue: Food Control
nodes.abstract: Fruit ripening is a complex physiological process that determines fruit quality and influences consumer acceptance. Among the various indicators of ripeness, visual appearance plays a decisive role, as it is the first attribute perceived and often defines expectations regarding flavor, freshness, and overall quality. However, conventional maturity assessment frequently relies on analytical procedures that require destructive sampling, are time-consuming, or have limited applicability for real-time and large-scale monitoring. In this context, this review critically examines the potential of visual biomarkers to connect fruit ripening physiology, non-destructive sensing, predictive modeling, and sensory quality. A bibliometric mapping identifies major research trends, while the critical synthesis distinguishes instrumental quality prediction, associations with sensory attributes, and direct prediction or validation of consumer-relevant outcomes. The review integrates the biochemical foundations of ripening with practical approaches, examining how changes in pigments, sugars, texture, and other ripening-related attributes are translated into measurable visual and spectral features. Imaging and sensing technologies, including RGB, near-infrared, hyperspectral, and thermal approaches, are discussed alongside image processing, chemometrics, and machine learning. Although these technologies can achieve strong performance in maturity classification and physicochemical quality prediction, high instrumental predictive accuracy does not necessarily establish sensory relevance. Sensory evaluation can address this gap either by providing prediction targets or by serving as an independent reference for validating whether instrumentally detected changes correspond to perceived quality. Overall, standardized protocols, external validation, model transferability, and sensory integration from the experimental design stage are needed to advance robust and consumer-relevant fruit ripeness prediction.

nodes.name: Towards zero-waste cities: Insights from building material waste flow mapping and stakeholder engagement in Montréal
nodes.venue: Sustainable Futures
nodes.abstract: Montréal is among numerous cities pursuing zero-waste objectives aligned with global sustainability goals. Construction, renovation, and demolition (CRD) waste represents a significant component of urban waste streams and offers substantial opportunities for reduction through circular economy (CE) strategies and innovative material management approaches. Achieving zero-waste urban resource management requires an integrated understanding of three key dimensions: (1) the characterization of CRD materials, (2) the infrastructure supporting CRD waste management, and (3) stakeholder dynamics within the building sector and their interactions with CRD materials across the life cycle. However, data describing these dimensions remain fragmented, limiting the implementation of CE practices and evidence-based policy and planning decisions. This paper presents Montréal as a critical case study demonstrating how qualitative and quantitative CRD data can be integrated and visualized to create an exploratory data-integration and stakeholder-informed mapping framework for urban resource management. The study combines a literature review, semi-structured interviews, field observations, thematic analysis, and data visualization methods to spatialize and map CRD flows. The objectives are to characterize CRD waste and its spatial distribution, identify key stakeholders and their roles throughout the CRD waste life cycle, and determine challenges and opportunities for policy intervention. Results indicate that Montréal recovers 42% of CRD materials, while the remainder is landfilled. Stakeholder analysis revealed that 65% of interviewees are involved in end-of-life activities, while material classification, intersectoral collaboration, and financial incentives emerged as key challenges influencing CE implementation. Findings highlight the need for coordinated stakeholder engagement and data-driven decision-making to advance towards zero-waste.

nodes.name: SpectralGuard: a Spectrally grounded λ-SHAP framework for XAI validity certification in pharmaceutical supply chain networks
nodes.venue: Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence
nodes.abstract: Permutation-based explainability methods such as SHAP are central to regulatory compliance in AI-governed pharmaceutical supply chains across Sub-Saharan Africa, yet their validity depends on a structural property that existing frameworks do not monitor: the algebraic connectivity of the supply hypergraph, quantified by the Fiedler eigenvalue λ 2 . We prove that λ 2 → 0 is a sufficient condition for permutation-based XAI failure (Theorem 3.5): no increase in sampling effort can recover validity once network connectivity collapses. We introduce SpectralGuard, demonstrated on a calibrated synthetic DGP driven by real Eskom load-shedding and SARB ZAR/USD records ( n = 3, 227 business days, 2014–2026); all spectral results are from the synthetic hypergraph. λ-SHAP shrinks attributions toward a fluid-regime prior using λ 2 ( t ) as the shrinkage weight, maintaining auditability at an explicit bias–variance cost (Remark 3.12). A probabilistic validity certificate V ( t ) combines four spectral metrics with SHA-256 tamper-evidence. An oracle experiment ( B = 500, Seed = 2,026) demonstrates 70.4–89.2% attribution MSE reduction across governance regimes. The spectral gate is the decisive ablation component. In the synthetic DGP, early-warning detection leads classical baselines by 19 business days (λ c alert preceding the λ m crossing). Field validation on real CCMDD procurement data is planned for 2027 (PLMIF-2). A nine-step DHIS2 integration pathway supports SDG 3, 9, 13, and 16.

nodes.name: Real-time state-of-health estimation and online degradation prognosis from partial battery discharge using Physics-Informed Neural Networks
nodes.venue: Journal of Power Sources
nodes.abstract: With the increasing integration of renewable energy sources, energy storage systems have become essential, making the accurate estimation of their State of Health (SOH) and degradation behavior critical. In this work, we propose a physics-informed deep learning approach for lithium-ion battery SOH prediction using incomplete discharge curves extracted from arbitrary voltage ranges, thereby reflecting realistic and heterogeneous operating conditions. The proposed method combines data-driven learning with physically motivated degradation dynamics to ensure consistent and reliable SOH estimation from partial discharge information, achieving a MAPE below 4$\%$. In addition, a real-time degradation trend estimation strategy is introduced to detect key aging transitions without requiring prior knowledge or historical data, making it applicable to a wide range of batteries. Overall, our approach enables SOH estimation from arbitrary discharge segments and a real-time degradation forecast that continuously integrates all usage, overcoming previous methods that rely on fixed protocols or early, non-adaptive predictions.

nodes.name: QUARTZ: Qualitative Understanding via Accessible Representation and Visualization
nodes.venue: International ACM SIGACCESS Conference on Computers and Accessibility (ASSETS)
nodes.abstract: Qualitative data visualizations – concept maps, network graphs, Sankey diagrams, and coding stripes – are integral to research practice, yet remain entirely inaccessible to blind and low-vision (BLV) researchers. While visualization has seen advanced multimodal solutions for quantitative charts, qualitative visualizations, and their non-linear, semantically rich structures have received no attention. We present QUARTZ, a web-based system that provides screen-reader-accessible, multimodal representations of qualitative data visualizations. Using the Rapid Iterative Testing and Evaluation (RITE) method, we conducted a formative user study with 8 BLV participants who completed 12 tasks across four visualization types. Our findings expose accessibility barriers unique to qualitative visualizations, non-linear navigation breakdowns and semantic comprehension gaps absent from quantitative chart research, and document how iterative co-design with BLV users progressively addressed them across sessions. We contribute empirical evidence and design guidelines for an underexplored visualization domain, advancing the infrastructure BLV researchers need to participate independently in qualitative inquiry.

nodes.name: International ACM SIGACCESS Conference on Computers and Accessibility (ASSETS)
Net primary productivity in the Gulf of California: spatio-temporal patterns and drivers in a warming climate (2003–2024)
nodes.venue: Ocean science
nodes.abstract: Abstract. The Gulf of California is a highly productive and diverse ecosystem that supports nearly 70 % of Mexico's fisheries. Despite its ecological and socio-economic importance, basin-scale analysis of seasonal and interannual variability in net primary productivity (NPP). This study analyses 22 years (2003–2024) of satellite-derived NPP data to identify its main spatiotemporal patterns and environmental drivers. The monthly climatology reveals that the cold season (December–May) accounts for 68 % of the annual NPP, while the warm season (June–November) contributes only 32 %. To characterize regional variability, we applied the k-means++ clustering algorithm, and validated the resultant classification using discriminant analysis. This procedure robustly identified three productivity zones: high (HPZ; > 1700 mg C m-2 d-1), mid (MPZ; 900–1700 mg C m⁻² d⁻¹), and low (LPZ; < 900 mg C m-2 d-1). Interannually, the HPZ contributes 61.4 % of total NPP despite occupying only 30 % of the gulf’s area, whereas the LPZ covers 36 % of the area but produces just 16.9 %. A significant negative anomaly between 2013 and 2019 led to a 9 % decline in NPP relative to the long-term mean (124 Tg C y-1), a period coincided with intense warming episodes, including multiple marine heatwaves and the strong 2015–2016 El Niño. A partial recovery occurred between 2020 and 2024. The dominant environmental drivers of NPP differ among zones: sea surface temperature and mixed-layer depth control NPP in the HPZ, temperature and euphotic zone depth in the MPZ, and euphotic depth and phosphate availability in the LPZ. Overall, our analysis demonstrates that anomalously warm years compress the spatial extent of productive zones. Continued warming and stratification are therefore likely to expand oligotrophic conditions, increasing the area of low-productivity waters with profound ecological consequences for the Gulf of California.

nodes.name: How ENSO controls the propagation speed of seasonal onsets in Java–Bali: satellite rainfall evidence over two decades
nodes.venue: Journal of Southern Hemisphere Earth System Science
nodes.abstract: Indonesia, as a tropical maritime continent, exhibits a seasonal rainfall pattern influenced by the El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO). Variations in the Wet Season Onset (WSO) and Dry Season Onset (DSO) have broad implications for agriculture, water resources and disaster mitigation. This study aims to analyse the climatology and interannual variability of WSO and DSO over the Java–Bali region (104–116°E), using satellite-based rainfall data (1998–2024). The results show a clear monsoonal pattern, with maximum (minimum) rainfall from December to February (June to August). Climatologically, WSO (DSO) propagates eastward (westward) at ~21 km day–¹ (19 km day–¹) with an onset difference of ~57 (64) days between western Java and Bali. WSO is coherent across all four regions, whereas DSO is coherent across three Java regions (weaker coherence with Bali), consistent with a stronger and more spatially uniform ENSO relationship for WSO. Despite the ENSO predictability barrier, DSO remains significantly related to the Relative Oceanic Niño Index (RONI), with earlier DSO associated more strongly with the developing positive ENSO than with the decaying event from the preceding wet season. El Niño accelerates westward propagation of DSO, whereas La Niña slows DSO and WSO propagation. For WSO, El Niño delays the onset timing with propagation speed comparable with climatology, whereas La Niña advances onset with slower progression. Hence, ENSO affects seasonal onset timing and modulates the longitudinal propagation pace of monsoonal systems. These findings highlight monsoon spatio-temporal propagation as a key atmospheric response to ENSO over Java–Bali, with implications for climate prediction, agricultural planning and hydrometeorological risk management.

nodes.name: Journal of Southern Hemisphere Earth System Science
Evaluating the performance and reliability of CA-Markov and CA-ANN models for land use/land cover change simulation in Southwestern Nigeria
nodes.venue: Discover Geoscience
nodes.abstract: Accurate Land Use/Land Cover Change (LULCC) modelling and forecasting are crucial for understanding environmental dynamics and guiding sustainable land management in rapidly urbanising regions. This study compares the predictive accuracy and reliability of two hybrid models, Cellular Automata–Markov (CA–Markov) and Cellular Automata–Artificial Neural Network (CA–ANN) for Southwestern Nigeria. Reliability was assessed as a composite measure combining statistical agreement (accuracy and kappa), spatial consistency (pattern agreement between simulated and observed maps), and class-level stability (persistence of landcover categories over time). Multi-temporal Landsat imagery (2002, 2012, and 2022) was classified and processed in TerrSet’s Land Change Modeller using four GIS-derived drivers: distance to roads, distance to rivers, slope, and elevation. Transitional potentials were calibrated on 2002–2012 and validated against the observed 2022 map. Built-up land increased by over 340%, while wetlands declined by 47%, indicating rapid urban expansion. Accuracy assessment showed CA-Markov (Kappa = 0.846, overall accuracy = 89.4%) outperformed CA-ANN (Kappa = 0.707, overall accuracy = 78.9%), with discrepancies exceeding 15% in simulated areas and 10% in spatial allocation most pronounced in built-up and wetland classes. CA–Markov slightly overestimated urban growth, whereas CA–ANN underestimated built-up expansion and showed greater misclassification, particularly higher emission errors for built-up and water classes. CA-Markov provided the more reliable simulation under these conditions, while CA-ANN requires additional driving variables and parameter optimisation. The study underscores the value of integrated statistical, spatial, and class-level evaluation for LULCC model assessment to support land management and sustainable development planning in Southwestern Nigeria.

nodes.name: Enhanced cotton leaf disease classification Through ConvNeXt and Random Walk Grey Wolf Optimization
nodes.venue: Discover Artificial Intelligence
nodes.abstract: India has the highest number of cotton-cultivated land globally, thus placing it among the biggest producers of cotton in the world. Despite the huge cotton production, cotton leaf diseases still remain one of the most significant causes of yield losses in the crop. Accurate and early diagnosis is one of the first steps towards finding the solutions to mitigate the effects of the disease. In this research paper, we present the ConvNeXt deep learning framework used along with Random Walk Grey Wolf Optimizer (RWGWO) to diagnose and classify various diseases in cotton leaf. In its performance, ConvNeXt shows better accuracy when compared to the traditional CNN, Self-Organizing Map Artificial Neural Networks (SOMANN), Support Vector Machine (SVM) and other hybrid models with classification accuracy of 98.39%. Among others, our model successfully diagnoses and classifies the diseases of bacterial blight and aphid infestation, powdery mildew, armyworm, target spot, and healthy cotton leaves. All this is possible through a carefully chosen data set with proper data augmentation. The results of this research indicate that there is a high potential in using deep learning technology to improve agribusiness and textile fibers supply chain through early detection and management of the diseases outbreaks, which reduces the waste of pesticides associated with the late disease diagnosis. On the other hand, it should be noted that the use of ConvNeXt has limitations since larger models of this framework (ConvNeXt-Large and ConvNeXt-XL) have high computational complexity and energy consumption. The future work will include using field data sets and implementation of multi-modal learning, which will take into consideration various environmental factors.

nodes.name: Emerging paradigm in sensor based pedology: Advances, applications, challenges and future perspectives
nodes.venue: Plant Science Today
nodes.abstract: Pedology has seen a significant revolution due to the adoption of modern sensors that can provide fast, non-invasive and high resolution measurements of soils. Traditional pedological surveys that rely on field work and laboratory analysis are efficient, yet time consuming, cumbersome and have exhibit low spatial resolution. Modern advancements in sensors that measure optical, geophysical, elemental, moisture and remote sensing characteristics of soils have considerably improved the evaluation of soil’s physical, chemical and morphological characteristics. This article provides a detailed overview of emerging sensor-based techniques in pedology including the principles of these techniques, their applications and limitations. The review further examines the roles of digital soil mapping (DSM), proximal soil sensing, Geographic Information Systems (GIS), machine learning and artificial intelligence in enhancing soil property prediction and spatial modelling. This review also highlights the significance of calibration and validation of sensors and ground truthing of observations. It critically analyses the problems associated with the calibration transferability, soil heterogeneity, moisture effects and cost of sensors. Recent advances in sensor fusion, internet of things (IoT)-enabled monitoring, hyperspectral imaging and explainable artificial intelligence are also discussed as promising directions for future soil assessment. Furthermore, major research gaps including the need for standardised calibration protocols, regional soil spectral libraries, affordable sensing technologies and interpretable machine-learning models are identified. Overall, sensor-based pedology complements conventional soil survey methods by providing accurate, efficient and spatially continuous soil information thereby supporting sustainable soil management, precision agriculture, environmental monitoring and evidence-based land-use planning under changing climatic conditions.

nodes.name: Effects of Urban Blue–Green Landscape Patterns on Carbon Sequestration in Chongqing’s Central Urban Area: An XGBoost–SHAP Analysis
nodes.venue: Sustainability in Environment
nodes.abstract: Against the backdrop of the "Dual Carbon" goals, this study focused on the main urban area in Chongqing. With remote sensing, land use, meteorological data from 2000, 2010, and 2020 -- we used the CASA model to estimate vegetation net primary productivity, or NPP, which we compared to MODIS NPP products. By combining optimal scale analysis, landscape pattern indices, the XGBoost model and SHAP (the Shapley Additive exPlanations) interpretation methods, our study showed that the space relationship between the blue and green landscapes and how they help to reduce the amount of vegetation carbon sinks are associated with one another, not just by the space that the areas are in, but by these other ways. The results indicate that from 2000 to 2020, NPP in the study area showed an overall upward trend. High-value areas were primarily distributed in the peripheral mountains and continuous ecological spaces, while blue-green spaces in the central urban area and densely built river valleys exhibited greater fragmentation. Compared to the baseline model (M0) containing only elevation and slope, the extended model (M1) incorporating landscape pattern indices significantly improved cross-validation R² values: from 0.5954, 0.6248, and 0.5735 to 0.7996, 0.8031, and 0.7311 for the years 2000, 2010, and 2020, respectively.SHAP analysis revealed that among the selected predictors, elevation contributed the most. PLAND (Percentage of Landscape) demonstrated a significant predictive contribution across all three years, whereas the roles of ED (Edge Density), SPLIT (Splitting Index), and AI (Aggregation Index) varied interannually. Nonlinear responses and reference thresholds were identified for elevation, slope, PLAND, LPI (Largest Patch Index), and their contributions to NPP prediction; however, SHAP contributions do not imply direct causal effects. The study concludes that topographic backgrounds, combined with the area, fragmentation, and connectivity of blue-green spaces, collectively correlate with spatial variations in NPP within mountainous cities. These findings provide a reference for optimizing ecological spaces and enhancing vegetation carbon sink potential in the main urban area of Chongqing.

nodes.name: Detection-aware disparity refinement for weak-texture pavement target reconstruction in stereo vision
nodes.venue: Scientific Reports
nodes.abstract: Abstract Accurate detection and depth perception of pavement targets from close-range remote sensing observations are important for intelligent road monitoring and transportation infrastructure assessment. However, existing stereo matching methods often produce unstable disparity estimates in weak-texture and low-height pavement regions, such as manhole covers and speed bumps, where the disparity distribution is easily affected by matching ambiguity and image noise. To address this issue, a detection-guided disparity post-processing strategy named Detection-Aware Disparity Refinement (DADR) is proposed. A custom pavement dataset containing approximately 3000 annotated images is first constructed from a binocular vision-based remote sensing platform, covering five pavement target categories, including manhole covers, speed bumps, road damage, storm drains, and iron plates. YOLOv11 is employed to detect target regions, while FoundationStereo is used to generate initial disparity maps from calibrated stereo images. Instead of modifying the stereo matching network, the proposed method performs a rule-based post-processing operation that combines detection bounding boxes, a local ground-reference disparity, and confidence-weighted fusion to stabilize the disparity representation within detected target regions. Experimental results show that the YOLOv11 detector achieves a Precision of 0.89, a Recall of 0.88, and an mAP@50 of 0.895, and compares favourably with other one-stage detectors trained under the same protocol. Visual analysis with magnified regions of interest shows that the proposed strategy produces more spatially coherent disparity responses for weak-texture pavement targets, and an ablation study identifies the local ground reference and the adaptive confidence weighting as the main contributing components. Quantitative evaluation indicates that the within-region disparity standard deviation decreases from 3.81 px to 1.25 px after refinement. Because no independent depth ground truth is available, this result is reported as improved local disparity consistency rather than improved absolute depth accuracy. The proposed approach offers a lightweight, detector-agnostic disparity stabilization strategy for low-height pavement targets in close-range remote sensing scenarios and provides useful geometric cues for subsequent road-condition assessment, while its reliance on a locally planar ground reference and on detector reliability is discussed as a limitation.

nodes.name: Deformation‐Robust Multimodal Electronic Skin Enabled by Conformal Surface Plasmons for Cross‐Medium Robotic Perception
nodes.venue: Advanced Functional Materials
nodes.abstract: ABSTRACT Electronic skins (e‐skins) generally transduce contact mechanics but cannot interrogate materials concealed by packaging, limiting robotic perception to accessible surfaces. A multimodal cross‐medium e‐skin is developed by co‐designing a five‐channel piezoresistive network and a conformal surface‐plasmon (CSP) waveguide within a shared flexible interdigitated‐electrode architecture. The piezoresistive channel maps grasp pressure over 0–140 kPa with response and recovery times below 50 ms, whereas the CSP channel confines microwaves to a subwavelength near field for phase‐based pre‐touch sensing and frequency‐resolved electromagnetic fingerprinting. Strong field localization preserves transmission fingerprints under bending and twisting up to 80° and enables interrogation through glass, plastic, and paper containers. Coupled with a support vector machine, these fingerprints discriminate 16 sample classes with 99.4% test accuracy and 99.7% leave‐one‐out cross‐validation accuracy. When integrated with a dexterous robotic hand, the platform unifies grasp‐pressure mapping, proximity perception, and nondestructive recognition of hidden contents. This shared‐architecture strategy transforms conformal plasmonic waveguides into deformation‐tolerant functional sensing interfaces and extends e‐skin beyond contact‐limited tactile sensing toward cross‐medium robotic perception.

nodes.name: Characterizing geospatial access to comprehensive breast cancer services in Northern Tanzania
nodes.venue: Frontiers in Oncology
nodes.abstract: Background Tanzania has a high breast cancer mortality burden attributed in part to poor access to comprehensive cancer services. The objective of this study was to characterize geospatial patterns of breast cancer patients presenting to the only tertiary hospital in northern Tanzania that provides comprehensive breast cancer care. Methods This geospatial analysis used baseline data from adult breast cancer patients diagnosed at Bugando Medical Center (BMC) in Mwanza, Tanzania, between July 2019 and December 2023. Participants were geocoded to their residential subdistricts as defined by the United States Census Bureau. Forty-five subdistricts in the catchment area were identified as the spatial unit of analysis. Age-standardized observed rates depicted the number of patients diagnosed with breast cancer per subdistrict. Global and local Moran’s I statistics assessed spatial autocorrelation of observed breast cancer rates. Ordinary least squares regression models evaluated community-level factors, including population density, the presence of hospitals, and distance to comprehensive cancer care. Results We included 379 women diagnosed with breast cancer from the catchment area, with a median of 3 breast cancer cases per subdistrict (IQR: 0-10). Participant ages ranged from 21–90 years old. The mean age-standardized observed breast cancer rate was 4.2 per 100,000 women (IQR: 0-10.1). Observed breast cancer rates were spatially clustered across the entire catchment area (Moran’s Index= 0.289; p=0.001). Additionally, specific subdistricts where clustering and dispersion existed were identified. Ordinary least squares regression identified community-level factors (low population density; p=0.003, greater distance to BMC; p<0.001) associated with lower breast cancer rates. Conclusions We identified spatial clustering of breast cancer rates in the Northern region of Tanzania. Spatial clustering aligned with distance to comprehensive cancer care and population density, suggesting that low observed rates in remote areas may reflect underdiagnosis due to diagnostic availability rather than lower disease burden. Decentralizing diagnostic capacity, particularly in low-rate spatial clusters, may enhance equitable access to care for patients facing geographic barriers and improve breast cancer early detection and outcomes.

nodes.name: Characterizing Climate-Driven Shifts in Chilean Rainfall Regimes with a Hybrid Hidden Markov–Copula Framework
nodes.venue: Hydrology and earth system sciences
nodes.abstract: Abstract. Chile's hydroclimate exhibits pronounced meridional gradients and strong interannual variability, posing persistent challenges for regime-aware, probabilistic rainfall prediction. We introduce a hierarchical framework that explicitly separates large-scale regime dynamics from local spatial dependence. The approach integrates: (i) a covariate-driven non-homogeneous Hidden Markov Model (nHMM) to learn synoptic precipitation regimes and their transitions; (ii) Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) clustering to delineate precipitation-coherent climatic zones; and (iii) state-conditional Regular Vine copulas with Generalized Pareto (GPD) tails to model residual spatial dependence and extremes. The analysis employs the 0.05° daily CR2MET precipitation product over continental Chile (462 grid points, May–August 1980–2021) together with large-scale atmospheric covariates including the Southern Oscillation Index (SOI), the Oceanic Niño Index (ONI), and Global Mean Sea-Surface Temperature (GMSST). Five physically consistent rainfall regimes emerge, spanning from an anticyclonic dry state to a cyclonic wet state, confirmed by composites of mean sea-level pressure, 850-hPa winds, and 500-hPa geopotential height. Mixed-effects inference on the transition matrix reveals a statistically significant decline in wet-state persistence of ~0.34 % yr-1 (≈14.5 % over 1980–2022), coincident with rising GMSST. Out-of-sample ensembles for 2022 (100 daily members conditioned on Viterbi states) are well calibrated: central 90 % prediction intervals achieve near-nominal coverage, low asymmetry, and widths increasing southward with climatological variance. By disentangling regime timing and drivers from residual spatial co-variability and extremes, the proposed nHMM – DTW – vine – GPD framework yields meteorologically coherent states, spatially consistent probabilistic simulations, and quantitatively validated forecasts. The method is computationally tractable and transferable, offering a principled pathway for regime-conditioned, uncertainty-aware precipitation prediction to support hydroclimate risk management in Chile and other topographically complex regions.

nodes.name: CSFS-YOLOv8n landslide detection dataset and code (Jialin County, Xizang)
nodes.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
nodes.abstract: This dataset accompanies the manuscript CSFS-YOLOv8n: A Complex Terrain Landslide Detection Model Synergistically Enhanced by SCConv and SCSA (PLOS ONE). It contains the self-acquired UAV-derived landslide detection data collected by our team in Jialin County, Xizang, China: dataset/images: UAV landslide image tiles (DJI Zenmuse L1, 5472x3648 px), organized as train/val/test (84 images derived from 17 original frames, split at the original-frame level to prevent data leakage) dataset/labels: YOLO-format annotations (class 0 = landslide) dataset/splits: train/val/test file lists dataset/data.yaml, README, LICENSE (CC BY 4.0): dataset configuration and documentation code: source code of CSFS-YOLOv8n (modified Ultralytics YOLOv8 v8.2.103 with SCConv and SCSA modules, AGPL-3.0), including training/validation/inference entry scripts and the final model weights (best.pt) used in the paper Third-party datasets analyzed in the paper are publicly available from their original sources: the Bijie landslide dataset (http://gpcv.whu.edu.cn/data/Bijie_pages.html) and the CAS landslide dataset including the Jiuzhaigou and Moxi Town sub-datasets (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.10294997). The Medog sub-dataset cannot be shared due to national regulatory restrictions on high-resolution remote sensing data covering border areas; it was used only as an independent cross-regional generalization test set.
